generating-functional-persistence-c323db.title: Vacuum Persistence Amplitude
generating-functional-persistence-c323db.interpretation: Defines the generating functional as the total probability amplitude for a field to remain in the vacuum state under the influence of an external source J.
generating-functional-persistence-c323db.symmetry_origin: The master variational functional for quantum fields, encapsulating all possible vacuum fluctuations.
generating-functional-persistence-c323db.limits_and_boundary: The normalization factor $Z[0]$ represents the vacuum amplitude in the absence of sources.

lepton-flavor-doublet-structure-d3e0fd3a.title: Lepton Flavor Doublets
lepton-flavor-doublet-structure-d3e0fd3a.interpretation: Organizes the left-handed leptons into weak isospin doublets that transform under the (2)_L$ gauge group.
lepton-flavor-doublet-structure-d3e0fd3a.symmetry_origin: The electroweak symmetry requirement that acts specifically on chiral field components.
lepton-flavor-doublet-structure-d3e0fd3a.limits_and_boundary: Defines the coupling pattern for all charged-current weak interactions.

euler-lagrange-equations-dcda7a85.title: Euler-Lagrange Equations of Motion
euler-lagrange-equations-dcda7a85.interpretation: The fundamental second-order differential equations that determine the path of a classical mechanical system. They guarantee that the path taken by the system extremizes (makes stationary) the action functional over time.
euler-lagrange-equations-dcda7a85.symmetry_origin: Constructed from Hamilton's Principle of Stationary Action, ensuring coordinate covariance under arbitrary point transformations on the configuration manifold.
euler-lagrange-equations-dcda7a85.limits_and_boundary: For conservative systems with Cartesian coordinates, they simplify directly to Newton's second law, F = ma.

electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.title: The Covariant Electromagnetic Stress-Energy Tensor
electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.interpretation: \( T^{\mu\nu} \) is the stress-energy tensor, \( F^{\mu\nu} \) is the electromagnetic field tensor containing electric and magnetic fields, and \( \mu_0 \) is the vacuum permeability.
electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.symmetry_origin: Gauge invariance and Lorentz invariance of the electromagnetic Lagrangian.
electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.limits_and_boundary: The trace of this tensor is identically zero (\( T^\mu_{\ \mu} = 0 \)) in four dimensions, reflecting the scale invariance of classical electromagnetism (light is massless).

T^{\\mu\\nu}.name: Electromagnetic Stress-Energy Tensor
T^{\\mu\\nu}.description: The tensor describing energy and momentum distribution in the fields.

F^{\\mu\\alpha}.name: Electromagnetic Field Tensor
F^{\\mu\\alpha}.description: The antisymmetric tensor containing field components.

g^{\\mu\\nu}.name: Spacetime Metric Tensor
g^{\\mu\\nu}.description: The metric tensor of the spacetime manifold.

\\mu_0.name: Vacuum Permeability
\\mu_0.description: The magnetic constant of free space.

electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.conceptual_definition: This tensor represents the energy density, momentum flux, and shear stress of the electromagnetic field in a covariant relativistic format, constructed using the field strength tensor \( F^{\mu\nu} \) and the metric tensor \( g^{\mu\nu} \).
electromagnetic-stress-energy-tensor-ide.intuitive_summary: The energy, momentum, and pressure of light are organized into a single symmetric matrix that determines how electromagnetism curves spacetime.

chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.title: Chandrasekhar Mass Limit Relation
chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.interpretation: \( M_{\text{Ch}} \) is the limit mass, \( \mu_e \) is the mean molecular weight per electron, and \( m_H \) is the mass of a hydrogen atom.
chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.symmetry_origin: Represents the balance between the outward relativistic quantum degeneracy pressure of electrons and the inward pull of Newtonian gravity.
chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.limits_and_boundary: As the gravitational constant \( G \to 0 \), the maximum mass goes to infinity. As the electron density parameter \( \mu_e \) increases (fewer electrons per nucleon), the maximum mass decreases.

M_{\\text{Ch}}.name: Chandrasekhar Limit Mass
M_{\\text{Ch}}.description: The maximum mass of a degenerate star supported by electron pressure.

c.name: Speed of Light
c.description: The speed of light in vacuum.

\\mu_e.name: Mean Molecular Weight per Electron
\\mu_e.description: The average number of nucleons per electron.

m_H.name: Hydrogen Atom Mass
m_H.description: The mass of a hydrogen atom, serving as a proxy for nucleon mass.

chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.conceptual_definition: This is the fundamental physical formulation of the Chandrasekhar limit \( M_{\text{Ch}} \), derived from quantum mechanics (\( \hbar \)), relativity (\( c \)), gravitation (\( G \)), and nuclear physics (\( m_H, \mu_e \)).
chandrasekhar-limit-88f98df2-31bbfff0-c5.intuitive_summary: The maximum mass of a degenerate star is determined by a combination of the Planck mass, the mass of a hydrogen atom, and the number of electrons per nucleon.
